title: Review: Pathogens and transmission; Nucleotides, DNA and RNA structure; DNA replication
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM10a#t2 term and clue written for the game; BM10a#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; GE01a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM10a#N.11a, GE01a#N.6a, IM01a#N.5, BM10a#N.2a, GE01a#N.2a, BM10a#N.12a, GE01a#N.4a, BM10a#N.8, GE01a#N.8, BM10a#N.9. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Deoxyribose
items.clue: The 5-carbon sugar found in the monomers of DNA

items.label: Uracil
items.clue: Base found in RNA in place of T; it pairs with A

items.label: Interphase
items.clue: Period before a cell divides, in which its DNA is copied.

items.label: DNA polymerase
items.clue: Enzyme that joins nucleotides to each other to build the new strand.

questions.stem: Which row correctly gives differences between DNA and RNA?

options.text: DNA: two strands, deoxyribose, thymine. RNA: two strands, ribose, uracil.
DNA: two strands, deoxyribose, thymine. RNA: one strand, deoxyribose, thymine.
DNA: two strands, ribose, thymine. RNA: one strand, deoxyribose, uracil.
DNA: two strands, deoxyribose, thymine. RNA: one strand, ribose and uracil.

questions.explanation: DNA is double-stranded, contains the pentose deoxyribose and has thymine; RNA is single-stranded, contains ribose and has uracil in place of thymine.

questions.stem: During replication, a section of a template strand with the base sequence TACGGA is copied. Which statement describes the new strand built on this section?

options.text: Its sequence is TACGGA, an exact copy of the template strand it was assembled on.
Its sequence is AUGCCU, because uracil replaces thymine in each newly made strand.
Its sequence is ATGCCT, held to the template by covalent bonds made by DNA polymerase.
Its sequence is ATGCCT, the complement of the template, held to it by hydrogen bonds.

questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G with C, so the new strand reads ATGCCT and is held to the template by hydrogen bonds between paired bases.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly explains how prions cause disease?

options.text: Prions are tiny viruses; their nucleic acid takes over brain cells and makes more prions.
The prion form has a different amino acid sequence from the normal protein, so it folds differently.
A β-sheet-rich form makes normal copies refold the same way; the aggregates damage brain cells.
Prions are destroyed by thorough cooking, so infection from food comes only from raw meat.

questions.explanation: The misfolded form converts normal prion protein; the aggregates build up, causing neurodegenerative disease such as CJD.

questions.stem: Which is a correct description of a single nucleotide?

options.text: A nitrogenous base only; the sugar and phosphate belong to the backbone.
A pentose sugar bonded to a phosphate group and to a nitrogenous base.
A phosphate group bonded to a nitrogenous base, which is bonded to a sugar.
A six-carbon sugar, glucose, bonded to a phosphate and to a base.

questions.explanation: A nucleotide has three components: a pentose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base. The sugar is central, with the phosphate and the base each bonded to it.

questions.stem: A cut in the skin heals as new skin cells are produced by cell division. Why must DNA replication take place before each of these divisions?

options.text: So that the existing DNA can be divided equally, half going to each of the new cells.
So that each new cell receives a complete copy of the DNA with an identical base sequence.
It does not need to take place, because replication is only required for reproduction.
So that the original DNA can stay intact in one cell and the other cell gets a new copy.

questions.stem: A solution of DNA is heated to 95 °C. The two strands separate, but each strand remains a continuous, intact chain of nucleotides. Which explanation is consistent with these observations?

options.text: The backbone of each strand is covalently bonded, so it survives heating that breaks the weaker hydrogen bonds between the strands.
The hydrogen bonds of the backbone are stronger than the covalent bonds between strands, so only the strands come apart.
Heating breaks the covalent bonds that join the two strands, while the hydrogen bonds within each strand stay intact.
The bases along each strand are covalently bonded to one another, which holds the strand together when the pairs separate.

questions.stem: A drug inhibits helicase but has no effect on DNA polymerase. What will happen to DNA replication in a cell treated with the drug?

options.text: Replication continues normally, because DNA polymerase unwinds the double helix itself as it copies each strand.
New strands are made but fall off the template, because helicase forms the hydrogen bonds that hold new bases in place.
Cell division continues without replication, because the existing DNA is simply shared between the two daughter cells.
Replication cannot begin, because the hydrogen bonds between the strands are not broken, so no template strand is exposed.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes how the two strands of a DNA double helix are held together?

options.text: By hydrogen bonds between identical bases, such as A with A, one on each strand
By covalent bonds between complementary bases, with one base on each strand
By hydrogen bonds between complementary bases, one base on each strand
By covalent bonds joining the sugar–phosphate backbones of the two strands

questions.explanation: The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases, one from each strand: adenine pairs with thymine and cytosine with guanine. The nucleotides within each strand are joined by covalent bonds.

questions.stem: A short section of a DNA molecule has one strand reading GATTC, paired base by base with a second strand reading CTAAG. The molecule is replicated once. Which statement describes the two DNA molecules produced?

options.text: Each is GATTC paired with CTAAG; each has one strand of the original molecule and one new strand.
Each is GATTC paired with CTAAG; one has both original strands and the other has two new strands.
One is GATTC paired with GATTC and the other is CTAAG paired with CTAAG.
One gets the bases GAT paired with CTA, and the other gets TC paired with AG.

questions.explanation: Each original strand was a template for a new, complementary partner. Both molecules match the parent, and each keeps one original strand: semi-conservative.

questions.stem: Analysis of a sample of double-stranded DNA from a hypothetical bacterium shows that 21% of its nitrogenous bases are adenine. What percentage of its bases are cytosine?
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so T = A = 21% and A + T = 42%. That leaves 100% − 42% = 58% for C and G together, and because C = G, cytosine is 58%/2 = 29%.
